title: Aranmula metal mirror
summary: A cast bronze disc is ground and polished by hand until its bare metal face gives a clear reflection, with no glass or silvering. The craft comes from a single village in Kerala, India, and the exact alloy mix is a closely held family skill.
howToPlay: Look at the master's sample: it shows the tone of metal you are aiming for.
Slide the alloy until your molten metal matches that tone, then press Cast.
Rub the cooled disc with the coarsest grit first, then change to a finer one, step by step.
When the face shines like a mirror, press Check to see your stars.
rules: Your score is one quarter alloy match and three quarters how much of the face is polished to a mirror.
A poor alloy leaves tiny pits in the cast that polishing can never remove.
Each grit only cuts while the surface is close to its own roughness, so you must work from coarse to fine.
Going back to a coarse grit on a smooth face scratches it again, and only a finer grit takes the scratches out.
Tilt the disc with the pointer to see the room reflected in a well polished face.
heritageNote: Aranmula mirrors are made in a village in Kerala, India, from a bronze alloy that is cast in a clay mould and polished by hand through finer and finer grits. The craft is protected as a regional product and is kept alive by a small number of families.
